subject: environmental-science

moments.title: Greta Thunberg's school strike
moments.body: On 20 August 2018, 15-year-old Greta Thunberg sits outside the Swedish parliament with a sign reading 'Skolstrejk för klimatet' (school strike for climate). The protest spreads. Fridays for Future becomes a global movement. The 20 September 2019 global climate strike draws an estimated 4 million participants in 161 countries.

quote.text: I want you to act as if the house is on fire. Because it is.

moments.takeaway: A teenager sitting alone outside parliament with a sign generated the largest environmental protest movement in history within 14 months.

now.title: Climate activism today
now.body: Extinction Rebellion (founded 2018) uses civil disobedience. Last Generation, Just Stop Oil, and similar groups extend confrontational tactics. Youth-led climate litigation (Held v. Montana 2023, Duarte Agostinho v. 32 states ECHR 2024) is producing legal precedent. Public protest fatigue and policing pushback are real factors.
now.open_questions: How do protest movements convert visibility into policy?

reflection: Thunberg sailed across the Atlantic in 2019 to avoid flying. The symbolism worked — and was widely mocked. Movement-building requires both symbolic action and theory of change.
